note: Banco Popular de Puerto Rico's credit card agreements, one per card, each read in full on 30 October 2026 as its card agreements page links them: Visa Cash Rewards, Visa PREMIA® Rewards, AAdvantage® Visa Signature Plus, JetBlue Mastercard, JetBlue Mastercard Eleva and Visa Cobalt Infinite, the six cards Popular's Virgin Islands site (popular.vi) offers, each issued by Banco Popular de Puerto Rico. Each card's purchase rate is 16.99% to 29.99% a year by creditworthiness (the Prime Rate plus a margin), written as that range; its cash advance rate 27.99% to 31.99%, written so. The cards that open at 1.99% a year for their first six months carry that as their introductory rate (Visa Cobalt Infinite and Visa Infinite have none); the 0% balance transfer offer isn't written, balance transfers not being modelled. Each card's annual fee is as its agreement states (none where it says $0). The cash advance and convenience check fee is 2% of each transaction, at least $2 and at most $10. The foreign transaction fee is 1% on the two Visa reward cards, 1.4% on the JetBlue Mastercard, and none on the others (written as 0). The minimum payment is 2% of the balance or the interest plus $10 or $29, whichever is higher (the whole balance when it's under $29): written as 2% with a $29 floor; the interest-plus-$10 alternative, the higher one when the month's interest and $10 together pass 2% of the balance, isn't modelled.The late fee is 'up to $40' (and never more than the minimum payment due) and the returned payment fee 'up to $10', each written at its stated top. The due date is at least 21 days after each statement closes, and purchases go without interest when the full balance is paid by it: no longest grace is stated, so none is written. The agreements state no penalty rate and no over-limit fee. The agreements' margin is set by creditworthiness for residents of Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands. The main banks in the US Virgin Islands are Popular, FirstBank and Oriental; FirstBank's site sits behind an Incapsula bot check, and Oriental's card disclosures answer 404 (30 October 2026), so neither is written. This file kept Popular's Visa Cash Rewards, read on 29 October 2026, and adds its terms in full and the other five cards. Wave 4 (30 October 2026): Oriental Bank files in the CFPB's database (Q2 2026) a revolving accounts agreement for its Mastercard in the US Virgin Islands (v5.2023), which sets the minimum payment at 2% of the balance or $15 but leaves the rates and fees to the card's disclosures; the only disclosures it files are its Puerto Rico ones (accurate as of July 2023, on an 8.50% prime rate, with a San Juan address), and no source read ties them to the Virgin Islands, so Oriental's cards aren't written. FirstBank's filed disclosures (accurate as of December 2025) don't mention the Virgin Islands either. So Popular stays the only bank written.
